column2: The judges' judging and famine frame a family's temporary residence in Moab's field; the wife and sons accompany the unnamed man before the naming verse.
column3: Live for a time renders sojourning rather than permanent ownership or citizenship.

column2: Abimelech, Naomi, Mahlon and Chilion are named as Bethlehem Ephrathites, with two sons and repeated Moab-field residence; the selected Abimelech is not changed to Elimelech.
Abimelech dies and Naomi remains with both sons; the explicit husband relationship is retained.
The sons take Moabite wives, Orpah and Ruth, and reside about ten years; the approximation is preserved.
Both sons also die, leaving the woman bereft of husband and two sons; the selected order recalls the husband before the sons in the loss summary.
She rises with both daughters-in-law and they return because they heard the Lord visited His people with bread; the plural hearing and repeated Moab field remain.
column3: Bread renders plural loaves collectively in the food-supply context, rather than specifying a count of individual loaves.

column2: Leaving the previous place with both daughters-in-law begins the road toward Judah; the return purpose remains explicit.
Each daughter-in-law is sent to her mother's house; the third-person wish about the Lord's mercy corresponds to their mercy toward the dead and Naomi.
column3: Mercy is shared across the comparative Greek clauses and repeated in English for clarity; this blessing addresses the women, not God with Thou.

column2: The grant and each woman's rest in a husband's house remain two linked wishes, followed by tender kissing, raised voice and weeping.
column3: This supplies an English object for the elliptical grant; the precise relation of the grant to the following rest remains open, without adding a named gift.

column2: Both women answer that they are returning with Naomi to her people; present are returning preserves their declared intention.
Naomi repeats the return command and questions whether sons remain in her womb to become their husbands; the bodily image and rhetorical negative remain.
Age prevents a husband, then the hypothetical hope of a husband and bearing sons leads into verse 13; no tonight is inserted.
column3: Even if is the inherited contextual interpretation of hoti eipa, not an explicit ei conditional. A closer for I said that I have hope construction and hypostasis's exact sense remain review questions.

column2: Waiting for sons to mature and refraining from marriage are separate questions, followed by a negative appeal, greater bitterness and the Lord's hand against Naomi.
column3: Against interprets en emoi in the adverse context; the comparison more bitter for me than for you remains as inherited.

column2: Raised voice and weeping recur, Orpah kisses and explicitly returns to her people, and Ruth follows Naomi; the selected return clause remains.
Behold introduces the sister-in-law's return to people and gods, and Naomi asks Ruth to follow; plural gods is retained.
Ruth's refusal to leave leads to paired journey/lodging and people/God commitments; ordinary you addresses Naomi. Authored lineation separates the parallel clauses without changing words.
column3: Do not oppose me by making me leave interprets the encounter/opposition verb with its infinitive; Ruth is not made to address God directly.

column2: Death-place and burial-place commitments precede the repeated oath formula and affirmative death shall part; authored lineation preserves the cadence.
column3: No only, if anything but, or negative is inserted into the final selected clause. The oath's precise logical relation through hoti remains unresolved.

column2: Naomi sees Ruth's firm resolve and ceases further speech to her; the English does not imply they never spoke again.
Both arrive in Bethlehem; the whole city's resounding reaction introduces the identity question Is this Naomi, without adding a specific emotion.
Naomi requests the translated name Bitter and attributes her bitterness to the Sufficient One, maintaining the repeated bitter wordplay.
column3: Hikanos as a divine title and the passive epikranthe with the Sufficient One as grammatical subject need further review; dealt bitterly with me is inherited interpretation, not an exhaustively established syntax.

column2: Full departure contrasts with empty return by the Lord; the name-question is followed by humiliation and affliction attributed to the Lord/Sufficient One.
Naomi and Ruth the Moabite daughter-in-law return from Moab's field and reach Bethlehem at the start of barley harvest.
column3: The singular returning participle can attach locally to Ruth or to the broader return description; the English repeats returned without changing the participants.

column2: Naomi has a man acquainted with her husband, mighty in strength and of Abimelech's kindred, named Boaz; acquaintance and kinship are both retained.
Ruth seeks leave to glean behind someone whose favour she finds, and Naomi answers Go, daughter; the eyes idiom remains.
She gleans behind reapers and happens upon Boaz's portion; by chance represents the repeated chance construction without adding a theological explanation.
Behold introduces Boaz from Bethlehem; the mutual blessings address reapers and Boaz while referring to the Lord in the third person.
Boaz asks his supervising servant whose young woman she is; the ownership/affiliation question is not replaced by a simple name request.
The supervisor identifies her as the Moabite girl who returned with Naomi from Moab's field, continuing his report into verse 7.
The report repeats her request to glean and gather among sheaves and states morning until evening with no rest even a little; no familiar shortened workday reading is substituted.
The opening negative question precedes two prohibitions on leaving for another field and an instruction to stay close to his maidens.
Eyes on the reaped field, following, behold, protection against touching and permission to drink from the servants' vessels remain in order.
Ruth falls facedown and bows, asking about favour and recognition despite being foreign; a foreign woman renders the final self-identification within the English question.
Fully told represents the emphatic report construction; care after her husband's death and leaving parents and birthplace for an unknown people both remain.
column3: Before renders yesterday and the third day as an idiom for prior acquaintance, not a claim about a literal two-day acquaintance threshold.

column2: Add the missing closing quotation mark after Boaz's blessing, before Ruth speaks in verse 13. His work/reward blessing and trust beneath the Lord's wings remain unchanged.
column3: This is a speech-boundary correction, not a claim that quotation marks are ancient Greek source tokens; the change follows the explicit speaker change in verse 13.

column2: Ruth asks favour of her human lord, acknowledges comfort and speech to her heart, then says affirmatively I shall be as one of your maidservants.
column3: No not is added to the final clause; handmaid and maidservants retain the inherited social vocabulary without a resolved slave/servant lexical study.

column2: Boaz invites bread and vinegar, heaps barley meal and Ruth eats to fullness with leftovers; barley meal is not replaced by roasted grain from another text.
As she resumes gleaning, Boaz permits gleaning even among sheaves and forbids shaming her; even marks the intensified permission.
Both repeated carry and cast constructions are rendered be sure, followed by leaving it, gleaning and no rebuke.
column3: The exact agricultural actions of bastazo/paraballo and the heaped material remain lexical questions; no automatic familiar pull-out-bundles paraphrase replaces them.

column2: Evening gleaning is followed by beating out and about an oiphi of barley; approximation and the source measure remain without a fixed modern conversion.
She carries the gleaning into the city, Naomi sees it, and Ruth gives her the food left after fullness; the gleaned grain and meal leftovers are distinct.
Naomi asks both where she gleaned and worked, blesses the one who noticed her, and hears Boaz's name; both notice/favour links remain.
Blessed of the Lord precedes mercy toward living and dead, then Naomi identifies the man's closeness and next-of-kin role.
column3: Lower-case he/his leaves open whether mercy's subject is Boaz or the Lord; the inherited dagger note is preserved and no pronoun capitalization resolves it here.

column2: Ruth reports staying close to his servants until all his harvest is complete; servants here remains distinct from maidens in the neighbouring instructions.
Naomi approves that Ruth went with his maidens and says they will not meet her in another field; the past movement and future encounter remain.
column3: The subject and hostile or neutral sense of meet require review; no harm or assault verb is inserted without a recorded decision.

column2: Ruth stays close to Boaz's maidens through barley and wheat harvest and lives with Naomi; the selected concluding residence notice remains.
column3: Until the harvest was over leaves the Greek singular harvest-finishing subject unspecified; Boaz or Ruth's activity may be intended and is not independently resolved here.
